+"""Provides a base class for log widgets which may follow the end of their content."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from textual.events import Resize
+from textual.message import Message
+from textual.reactive import var
+from textual.scroll_view import ScrollView
+
+
+class LogView(ScrollView):
+    """Base class for log widgets.
+
+    A log widget writes new content to the end, and *follows* that content (i.e. keeps
+    the end of the content in view) until the user scrolls back. Scrolling to the end
+    of the content will restore following.
+    """
+
+    auto_scroll: var[bool]
+    """Scroll to the end of the log when new content is written (defined in subclasses)."""
+
+    @dataclass
+    class FollowChanged(Message):
+        """Posted when a log widget starts or stops following the end of its content."""
+
+        widget: LogView
+        """The log widget which started or stopped following the end."""
+        is_following_end: bool
+        """Is the log widget following the end of its content?"""
+        scroll_y: float
+        """The vertical scroll position when the follow state changed."""
+        max_scroll_y: int
+        """The maximum vertical scroll position when the follow state changed."""
+
+        @property
+        def control(self) -> LogView:
+            """Alias for `widget`."""
+            return self.widget
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        name: str | None = None,
+        id: str | None = None,
+        classes: str | None = None,
+        disabled: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(name=name, id=id, classes=classes, disabled=disabled)
+        self._is_following_end = True
+        """Is the log following the end of its content?"""
+
+    @property
+    def is_following_end(self) -> bool:
+        """Is the log following the end of its content?
+
+        A log follows the end of its content until the user scrolls back, and will
+        follow it again when the user scrolls to the end. New content is only scrolled
+        in to view while the log is following the end.
+        """
+        return self._is_following_end
+
+    def follow_end(self, animate: bool = False) -> None:
+        """Scroll to the end of the log, and follow new content written to it.
+
+        Args:
+            animate: Animate the scroll to the end of the log.
+        """
+        self.scroll_end(animate=animate, immediate=True, x_axis=False)
+        self._set_following_end(True)
+
+    def _set_following_end(self, is_following_end: bool) -> None:
+        """Update the follow state, posting a message if it changed.
+
+        Args:
+            is_following_end: Is the log following the end of its content?
+        """
+        if is_following_end != self._is_following_end:
+            self._is_following_end = is_following_end
+            self.post_message(
+                self.FollowChanged(
+                    self, is_following_end, self.scroll_y, self.max_scroll_y
+                )
+            )
+
+    def _update_following_end(self) -> None:
+        """Update the follow state from the current scroll position."""
+        self._set_following_end(self.is_vertical_scroll_end)
+
+    def _should_follow_on_write(self, scroll_end: bool | None) -> bool:
+        """Should new content be scrolled in to view?
+
+        Args:
+            scroll_end: The `scroll_end` argument given to the write method, or `None`
+                to use [`auto_scroll`][textual.widgets.Log.auto_scroll].
+
+        Returns:
+            `True` if the log should scroll to the end, otherwise `False`.
+        """
+        auto_scroll = self.auto_scroll if scroll_end is None else scroll_end
+        return (
+            auto_scroll
+            and self._is_following_end
+            and not self.is_vertical_scrollbar_grabbed
+        )
+
+    def _stabilize_viewport(self, removed_lines: int) -> None:
+        """Keep the visible content stable after lines were removed from the start.
+
+        Does nothing if the log is following the end of its content, as the viewport
+        will be scrolled to the end anyway.
+
+        Args:
+            removed_lines: Number of lines removed from the start of the log.
+        """
+        if removed_lines and not self._is_following_end and self.scroll_y > 0:
+            scroll_y = max(0.0, self.scroll_y - removed_lines)
+            self.scroll_target_y = scroll_y
+            self.scroll_y = scroll_y
+            self.refresh()
+
+    def watch_scroll_y(self, old_value: float, new_value: float) -> None:
+        super().watch_scroll_y(old_value, new_value)
+        self._update_following_end()
+
+    def _on_resize(self, event: Resize) -> None:
+        if self._is_following_end:
+            # The viewport size has changed, so we may no longer be at the end.
+            self.scroll_end(animate=False, immediate=False, x_axis=False)
